Scanner: Programs That Listen

Read numbers and lines — including the famous newline trap, dodged on purpose.

⏱ 18 min🧠 No experience needed🧪 Interactive
Step 1

Tokens vs whole trays

nextInt grabs a token; nextLine scoops the tray.

💁

Curious cashier. After a number, a leftover newline crumb sits on the tray — the next scoop grabs the CRUMB, skipping your answer. One extra nextLine() eats it.

The Q&A program
import java.util.Scanner;

public class Main {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    Scanner in = new Scanner(System.in);
    System.out.print("Age: ");
    int age = in.nextInt();
    in.nextLine(); // eat the leftover newline crumb
    System.out.print("Name: ");
    String name = in.nextLine();
    System.out.println("Hi " + name + ", age " + age);
    in.close();
  }
}
// Sample run (you type 18 and Ada):
// Age: 18
// Name: Ada
// Hi Ada, age 18
Interactive: run it, type 18 then Ada. Watch the crumb get eaten on its own line.
Step 2

With vs without the fix

Same input, two fates.

What happens WITHOUT the extra line?

Predict, then reveal the skip.

Name reads "" — the leftover newline was “the answer”. The program never waits. One extra nextLine() after nextInt() fixes everything.
abc for nextInt()? InputMismatchException — crash. Peek with hasNextInt() first.
